samples: This program defines a shape type (circle, rectangle, or point) that only accepts positive dimensions, along with a way to compute each shape's area. It can produce a one-line description of a shape that includes its area, and it can pick the largest shape from a list, giving nothing for an empty list. Its entry point prints descriptions of three sample shapes and then names the largest, so it works as a small demo or a base for shape-measuring code rather than a full geometry library.

This module models plane shapes (circles, rectangles, and points) and checks that circle radii and rectangle sides are positive. It can produce a one-line description of a shape with its area, and it can pick the largest shape from a list, giving nothing for an empty list. Its `main` function prints descriptions of three sample shapes and then names the largest, using only the console and no other system access.

This program defines a shape type (circle, rectangle or point) whose circle and rectangle dimensions must be positive. It can work out each shape's area, write a one-line description with the area rounded to two decimals, and find the largest shape in a list, giving nothing for an empty list. Its main entry point prints descriptions of a few sample shapes and then names the largest, so it works as a small self-contained demo and a reusable shape-measuring module. It only needs console output and does no file or network access.

This program defines three kinds of plane shape (circle, rectangle, and point), where circles and rectangles must have positive dimensions, and it can compute each shape's area. It offers a function that turns a shape into a one-line description with its area rounded to two decimals, and another that picks the shape with the largest area (or nothing for an empty list). Its `main` prints descriptions of a sample set of shapes and then names the largest, needing only console access, so it works as a small self-contained demo and a reusable shape-measuring module.

This module defines three kinds of plane shape (circle, rectangle, and a point), where circles and rectangles must have positive dimensions, and it computes each shape's area (using 3.14159 for pi). It offers a function that produces a one-line description of a shape with its area rounded to two decimals, and another that finds the shape with the largest area, or nothing for an empty list. Its entry point simply prints descriptions of a sample circle, rectangle, and point, then names the largest, and it needs only console access, so it is a small, safe demo rather than a general geometry library.
